explanation: Store a pair (item,maximum-so-far) at every stack depth. Push computes the new maximum from the item and the previous top’s cached maximum; Pop removes one pair and GetMax reads the top pair’s second field.
correctness: By induction, each entry’s second field is the maximum of all items at or below that depth. Push extends this prefix maximum, and Pop reveals the already-correct maximum for the remaining prefix. Equal maxima need no special removal rule because every depth has its own snapshot.
walkthrough: Push 5 to store (5,5), then push 9 to store (9,9). GetMax reads 9 from the top pair. Pop returns its item 9 and removes that pair; GetMax now reads 5 from (5,5). Two pushes of 8 create two (8,8) entries, so one pop still leaves maximum 8. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh MaxStack. Push displays null; Pop/GetMax display integer results or {"error":"empty"}.
edgeCases: After pushing 8 twice and popping once, GetMax still returns 8. Empty Pop/GetMax raise an exception normalized to {"error":"empty"}.
timeComplexity: O(1) per operation under the stack push/pop cost model (amortized for dynamically grown arrays): only a constant number of stack operations occur.
spaceComplexity: O(s) persistent space for s live entries, including their stored maximum information.
